boundary: Concrete serialization and observability names for the approved contract; no additional operations, acceptance claims or authorization. Example paths/IDs/generation values are substituted from actual scratch state and open response.
run_state_note: Minimal guard-input excerpt, not a whole run_state schema fixture. Acceptance may embed it in a real-shaped scratch run_state. Controller reads this exact step_key; never writes the file.

schema_types.context: Object: optional working_dir, namespace, reader_config_ref, test_config_ref are nonempty strings; no extra keys. Empty object is valid.
schema_types.limits: Object: optional timeout_seconds is number >=0, output_bytes is integer >=1; no extra keys. Empty object is valid. Feature126 adds no timeout/wait semantics.
schema_types.payload: Object with expression as nonempty string for the stub examples. JSON expression is parsed as data, never Python evaluation.
schema_types.identity: Use schema principal objects and integer lease/attempt/counter values, never booleans or numeric strings. Copy actual generation and lease from open/transfer records.

request_variants.poll-operation: session_id, requester, expected_generation, expected_lease_epoch, operation_id only; current owner or lifecycle Orchestrator.
request_variants.transfer-session: session_id, requester, expected_generation, expected_lease_epoch, new_owner only; requester is lifecycle Orchestrator or current human owner. new_owner is the human or Generator principal object.
request_variants.close-session: session_id, requester, expected_generation, expected_lease_epoch only; lifecycle Orchestrator or current human owner.
request_variants.reopen: Use open_request fields with retained owner/contract_id/step_key/attempt/run_state_path, plus expected_generation and expected_lease_epoch from the prior session. Same session_id/root after correlated closure or crash; no reset of governed identity.
request_variants.human-submit: Replace requester with the current human owner object; all other required submit fields remain.

socket_framing: One UTF-8 JSON object plus newline per connection request; wrapper has exactly action and request. Response is one CLI response JSON object plus newline (no extra transport envelope). Trusted harness may inject a trial requester here to exercise supervisor refusal; this does not grant a trial an endpoint.
responses: Success {ok:true,result:RECORD}; failure {ok:false,error:REASON,result?:REJECTED_RECORD}. Public CLI trial denial is {ok:false,error:review_trial} with exit1 and no record write. Duplicate ID is {ok:false,error:conflict}, exit1, no overwrite. Other reason strings and exit codes follow the contract.
controller_metadata: Contains integer supervisor_pid, child_pid, supervisor_pgid; absolute string run_state_path; string contract_id, step_key; integer attempt. Other private fields may exist. Read after successful open. supervisor_pgid identifies the detached supervisor group, also containing its child, for bounded scratch cleanup. PID/group metadata is observability, never sufficient continuity proof.
child_receipt_note: Each received execute frame appends and flushes exactly this JSON-line receipt to child.stdout.log before stub execution. Lifecycle/init emits no such receipt. Logs may contain other diagnostics; tests parse receipt objects. Existing receipt lines survive reopen; compare counts/IDs before and after. Diagnostic output is bounded as contracted.
stub_results: set returns its assigned JSON value; get returns the stored JSON value for an existing name; gate completes with JSON null after the release file exists. Gate path lies inside the supplied scratch root. Missing-name behavior is not an acceptance obligation of this memo.
result_note: Result file is exactly the accepted child result frame as a JSON object, outside the operation schema record. It is absent while pending and for rejected operations; duplicate requests preserve existing bytes or absence. Operation records retain evidence_class:development.
fixture_harness_seam: tools/fixtures_self_test.sh defines runtime_session_checks() with a standalone closing brace. It invokes the nine commands in contract order (three checks, cases1/2/3, case8 policy, cases9/13), logs each exact command and actual exit, continues after failure, and returns nonzero if any command failed. The existing harness calls runtime_session_checks || fail=1. Independent tests may extract this actual function, substitute python3 in a scratch shell to log argv/inject one failure, and assert scheduling/return status without recursively executing the suite. No new CLI or semantics.
